questions.question: If house tax is paid before the due date, one gets a reduction of 12% on the amount of the bill. By paying the tax before the due date, a person got a reduction of ₹2,100. The amount (in ₹) of house tax was:
questions.solution:
Step 1   Scale back up. 
12% of bill = 2,100   ∴  bill = 2,100 / 12 × 100 = 
₹17,500

questions.question: A ₹750 tin of cheese is offered at 8% discount and a ₹1,250 tin of butter at 20% discount. If we buy 5 tins of cheese and 3 tins of butter, what is the effective discount we get (in %)? ₹750
questions.solution:
Step 1   Marked total of each item. 
cheese : 5 × 750 = ₹3,750        butter : 3 × 1,250 
= ₹3,750 
 Step 2   The two totals are equal, so the weights 
are 1 : 1. 
effective discount = (8 + 20) / 2 = 14%

questions.question: A ₹1000 box of cookies is offered at 10% discount and a ₹400 bar of chocolate is offered at 8% discount. If we buy 2 boxes of cookies and 3 bars of chocolate, what is the effective discount we get (in%)? ₹1000
questions.solution:
Step 1   Marked total of each. 
cookies : 2 × 1,000 = ₹2,000        chocolate : 3 × 
400 = ₹1,200   ⇒  5 : 3 
 Step 2   Alligation between 8% and 10% with 
those weights. 
3(x − 8) = 5(10 − x)   ⇒  8x = 74   ∴  x = 9.25%

questions.question: The marked price of an article is ₹550. A shopkeeper allows a discount of 20% and still gets a profit of 10%. If he sells it for ₹470, profit percent will be:
questions.solution:
Step 1   Selling price after the discount. 
550 − 20% = ₹440,  which carries 10% proﬁt   ∴  
CP = ₹400 
 Step 2   Now the new selling price. 
470 − 400 = ₹70 proﬁt   ⇒  70 / 400 × 100 = 
17.5%

questions.question: If an item has 12% discount on the marked price of ₹10,000 but the item is sold at ₹8,360 only, then what additional discount (in %) did the customer get?
questions.solution:
Step 1   What the first discount leaves. 
10,000 − 12% = ₹8,800 
 Step 2   The further cut, measured on 8,800. 
8,800 − 8,360 = ₹440   ⇒  440 / 8,800 × 100 = 
5%

questions.question: The marked price and the cost price of an article are in ratio 5:4. If the profit earned by selling the article is 12.5%, then what is the discount percentage?
questions.solution:
Step 1   MP : CP = 5 : 4, so take 50 and 40. 
12.5% of 40 = 5   ⇒  SP = ₹45 
 Step 2   Discount on the marked 50. 
5 / 50 = 10%

questions.question: A shopkeeper was offering two successive discounts of 20% and 15% on an item whose marked price is ₹1,000 while another shopkeeper was offering a flat 33% discount on the same item. Find the positive difference in the nominal amounts of discounts.
questions.solution:
Work the two offers separately in rupees, then 
compare. 
 Step 1   The successive pair. 
1,000 − 20% = 800,  − 15% = ₹680   ⇒  discount 
= ₹320 
 Step 2   The flat offer. 
1,000 − 33% = ₹670   ⇒  discount = ₹330 
 Step 3   Difference. 
330 − 320 = ₹10

questions.question: A retailer gives 40% discount on a certain article, and earns a profit of 25%. If the article costs ₹4,320 to the retailer, what is its marked price (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Write each relation as a ratio. 
40% off  ⇒  MP : SP = 5 : 3            25% profit  ⇒  
SP : CP = 5 : 4 
 Step 2   Equalise SP (LCM of 3 and 5 = 15). 
MP : SP : CP = 25 : 15 : 12 
 Step 3   CP is 12 parts. 
12 parts = 4,320 ⇒ 1 part = 360   ∴  MP = 25 × 360 
= ₹9,000

questions.question: A person bought an article at 30% discount on its marked price. The person then sold it at 30% profit for ₹427.70. What was the marked price of the article?
questions.solution:
Step 1   After a 30% discount he pays 7 units. 
CP = 7 units   ⇒  SP at 30% profit = 7 × 1.3 = 9.1 
units 
 Step 2   That is the ₹427.70. 
9.1 units = 427.70 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹47   ∴  MP = ₹470

questions.solution:
Step 1   Match every item to its category. 
tea ₹450 → groceries 12%     notebook ₹100 → 
stationery 15%     slipper ₹850 → footwear 20% 
 Step 2   Net value of each, then add. 
396 + 85 + 680 = ₹1,161

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought 80 kg of rice at a 10% discount. Also, 1 kg rice was offered free for every 20 kg purchased. If he sells the rice at the marked price, his profit percentage will be?
questions.solution:
Count what he PAYS for and what he SELLS 
separately — the free kilos are pure gain. 
 Step 1   Take the marked rate as ₹10/kg. 
cost = 80 × 10 × 0.9 = ₹720 
 Step 2   He receives 4 free kilos for the 80 bought. 
sells 84 kg at ₹10 = ₹840 
 Step 3   Profit. 
120 / 720 = 1/6 = 16⅔%

questions.question: In a scheme, a shopkeeper offers a 10% discount if you buy two or more books. Kiran buys two books for ₹540. If the shopkeeper still makes a 20% profit, find the profit he would make if he sold the books without the discount.
questions.solution:
Step 1   Marked total. 
MP = 540 / 0.9 = ₹600 
 Step 2   Cost price. 
CP = 540 / 1.2 = ₹450 
 Step 3   Profit if sold at the full marked price. 
600 − 450 = ₹150

questions.question: A shopkeeper pays 12% of the cost price as tax while purchasing an item whose cost is ₹500. He wants to earn a profit of 20% after giving a discount of 16% on the marked price. What should the marked price be?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Real cost to him. 
500 + 12% of 500 = ₹560 
 Step 2   The selling price he wants. 
SP = 560 × 1.20 = ₹672 
 Step 3   That is 84% of the marked price. 
MP = 672 / 0.84 = ₹800

questions.question: A person marks his 40 items at 20% above the cost price. He sells 10 items at 10% discount and 20 items at 15% discount. What is the maximum discount (rounded off) he can offer on the remaining items if he still gets some profit?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Prices per item. 
CP = 100, MP = 120;  total cost of 40 items = 
₹4,000 
 Step 2   What the first thirty bring in. 
10 × 108 = 1,080     20 × 102 = 2,040     ⇒  ₹3,120 
 Step 3   The last ten must beat the shortfall. 
4,000 − 3,120 = 880   ⇒  each above ₹88 
 Step 4   Turn that into a discount. 
(120 − 88)/120 = 26.67%  ⇒  the largest whole 
discount that still profits = 26%
